newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares finish lower in nervous trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares finish lower in nervous trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on Thursday in tense trading, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares fell 0.68 percent, or 1.76 points, to 258.19 on all-share turnover of 183 million shekels against 210 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.52 percent lower at 267.61.
"Trading was very volatile today and the market went up and down. Maof options speculators were simply rocking the market," said a trader at Bank Leumi.

"The market is very nervous and volatile, and it is not acting in a rational way. This seems to be only a very brief consolidation, which shows that the market is still very strong," said Michael Politzer, head of the economic department at the Central Securities Corp.

"The positive momentum is expected to continue and we keep waiting for a real correction, which never comes," the Leumi trader said. "Foreign investors were very busy buying today while options players were selling".
"Share prices rose very fast during the last few weeks. The market is expected to continue rising at a much slower pace," Politzer added.

Israel Discount Bank fell 1.25 percent to 415 agorot. Israel's parliamentary finance committee on Thursday gave the go-ahead for a secondary offering later this month of a 17 percent stake in the bank.
The government hopes to raise a minimum of 600 million shekels from the offering. Based on Discount's current market value, the offering is worth about 675 million shekels.

The most active shares were Israel Chemicals, which rose 3.0 percent to 399 agorot on volume of 11.2 million shekels; Supersol, which surged 4.25 percent to 1,043 agorot on turnover of 10.7 million shekels; and Bank Leumi, which fell 0.75 percent to 526 agorot on volume of 7.9 million shekels.
